chunks: The simile of those who take protectors besides Allah is that of the spider, who builds a house; and verily the weakest of houses is the spider's house, if they knew.

key_terms.لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ: If they knew (implying a call to reflection)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the spider metaphor in Surah Al-Ankabut?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a critique of both external political alliances and internal spiritual dependencies that distract from Tawhid (Divine Unity). The 'house' of the spider symbolizes the fragile structure of worldly attachments, which, unlike the firm foundation of God, collapse under the weight of divine judgment. This metaphor serves as a practical reminder for believers to anchor their trust solely in Allah, avoiding the illusion of security provided by created beings.
